title: Labyrinth (week 9)
description:
- Rooms are objects of class Room. name: name of the room, used whenever we print rooms. age: non-negative age of the room. doorsTo: rooms reachable through a door (one way only).
- A room is an exit if it has no doors. No null anywhere, finite, no directed cycles. Paths may merge again into the same room.
- Solution path: starts at the given room, follows doors, ends at an exit.
- You may ADD fields and methods to Room (paste your whole Room class below Labyrinth). Don't change name, age, doorsTo or isExit, and don't add constructors with parameters.

Rooms in the tests are called R0, R1, R2, …

questions.title: Print All Paths
questions.statement:
- Print every solution path starting at room, one per line.
- A path is printed as the names of its rooms, separated by spaces, e.g. A C F
- If room is already an exit, the path is just its name.

> What does the recursion need to remember?

**Method to write**
```
public static void printPaths(Room room)
```

**Examples** (labyrinth below)
```
printPaths(R0) prints (any order):
  R0 R1 R3
  R0 R2 R3
  R0 R4

printPaths(R3) prints:
  R3
```

questions.title: Print All Exits
questions.statement:
- Print the name of every exit that can be reached from room, one per line.
- Each exit exactly once, even if many paths lead to it.
- You may add fields to Room.

> Why is printing at the end of every path not enough?

**Method to write**
```
public static void printExits(Room room)
```

**Examples** (labyrinth below)
```
printExits(R0) prints (any order):
  R3
  R4
R3 is printed only once, although two paths lead to it.

printExits(R4) prints:
  R4
```

questions.title: Task 1: Prefix Sums
questions.statement:
- task1(room) returns true if some solution path has no prefix sum of ages divisible by 3.
- Ages [1, 1, 2] work (sums 1, 2, 4), ages [1, 2, 1] do not (second sum is 3).
- Work on your own for about 10 minutes, then we discuss.
- Hint: start from your solution to Exercise 1.

**Method to write**
```
public static boolean task1(Room room)
```

**Examples** (labyrinth below)
```
task1(R0) == false   R0 R1 R3 and R0 R2 R3 (ages 1 2 9) have sums 1, 3 (bad);  R0 R4 (ages 1 5) has sums 1, 6 (bad)

task1(R1) == true    R1 R3 (ages 2 9) has sums 2, 11

task1(R4) == true    sum 5

a single room with age 3:  task1 == false
```

questions.title: Path with Given Ages
questions.statement:
- Is there a solution path with exactly ages.length rooms whose ages are ages[0], ages[1], ...?
- Return true if such a path exists.
- Bonus: if such a path exists, print the names of its rooms.

> Which extra parameter does the recursion need?

**Method to write**
```
public static boolean hasPathWithAges(Room room, int[] ages)
```

**Examples** (labyrinth below)
```
hasPathWithAges(R0, {1, 2, 9}) == true

hasPathWithAges(R0, {1, 5})    == true

hasPathWithAges(R0, {1, 2})    == false   R1 / R2 are not exits

hasPathWithAges(R0, {1, 9})    == false   no door from R0 to R3

Bonus: hasPathWithAges(R0, {1, 5}) also prints  R0 R4
```

questions.title: Task 2: Same Ages, Different Rooms
questions.statement:
- task2(room): two solution paths of the same length with the same age at every position.
- At least one position holds different rooms (r_i != s_i).
- Two doors leading to the same room do not make two different paths.

> How is this like Exercise 4?

**Method to write**
```
public static boolean task2(Room room)
```

task2(R1) == false   only one solution path

questions.title: Unique Path from x to y
questions.statement:
- A path from x to y starts at x, follows doors and ends at y (y need not be an exit).
- Return true if there is exactly one such path.
- Rooms are compared by reference (==), not by age.

> Do we need to find all paths to answer this?

**Method to write**
```
public static boolean uniquePath(Room x, Room y)
```

**Examples** (labyrinth below)
```
uniquePath(R0, R3) == false   two paths (via R1 and via R2)

uniquePath(R0, R4) == true

uniquePath(R1, R3) == true

uniquePath(R3, R0) == false   no path at all (doors are one way)

uniquePath(R0, R0) == true    the path that is just R0

The real tests also use labyrinths with 2^60 paths, so trying all paths is too slow.
```

questions.title: Counting Paths
questions.statement:
- countPaths(x, y): number of paths from x to y.
- countExitPaths(x): number of solution paths from x.
- Return the result modulo 1 000 000 007.

> Why the modulo? Why does this only work without cycles?

**Method to write**
```
static final long MOD = 1_000_000_007;
public static long countPaths(Room x, Room y)
public static long countExitPaths(Room x)
```

**Examples** (labyrinth below)
```
countPaths(R0, R3) == 2

countPaths(R0, R0) == 1

countPaths(R3, R0) == 0

countExitPaths(R0) == 3

countExitPaths(R1) == 1

The real tests also use labyrinths with 2^70 paths, so plain recursion is too slow.
```

tests.name: countPaths: the example labyrinth: R0(1)->R1/R2/R4, R1(2)->R3, R2(2)->R3, R3(9), R4(5)   x = R0, y = R1

Room[] r = Lab.build(new int[]{1, 2, 2, 9, 5}, new int[][]{{1, 2, 4}, {3}, {3}, {}, {}});
check(Labyrinth.countPaths(r[0], r[1]), 1L);
